prompt: After a $25\%$ discount, a pair of shoes costs $\$60$. What was the original price, in dollars?
hint: The $\$60$ represents what fraction of the original price?

hints.text: The $\$60$ represents what fraction of the original price?

learningObjective: Reverse a percent change to recover the original amount.
explanation: A $25\%$ discount means the customer pays $75\%$ of the original price.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why adding 25% back fails
steps: Adding $25\%$ to $\$60$ gives $\$75$, which is one of the answer choices — and it is wrong.
The discount was $25\%$ of the *original*, not of the sale price, so the two percentages are taken from different bases.
Reverse percent questions are built entirely on this asymmetry. Always divide by the multiplier; never add the percent back.
